rubrics.justification: Generally captures a poor-quality, minimally cavitating embryo with absent discernible ICM/TE, consistent with 0DD, but overstates certainty about degeneration/apoptosis and calls it a compacted morula/very early blastocyst despite the provided Gardner designation and image suggesting an early blastocyst.

Integrates female age, ovarian reserve, endometrium, prior outcomes, and paternal age/sperm data with embryo quality reasonably well, though some links (stress effects, sperm DNA fragmentation inference) are somewhat speculative.

The logic is mostly consistent: very poor morphology drives a very low implantation estimate, moderated by favorable maternal age/endometrium. Minor issues include overcalling developmental delay on Day 4 and inferring specific mechanisms without direct evidence.

Broadly aligned in recognizing poor prognosis for a 0DD embryo and emphasizing counseling, but recommendations such as strongly recommending PGT-A at age 34 and a full RPL/thrombophilia/immune workup after one biochemical and one clinical miscarriage go beyond standard guideline-supported indications.

Provides clear counseling points and future-cycle options (consider sperm DNA fragmentation testing, culture to Day 5/6, review insemination method, lifestyle optimization), though some recommendations are not sufficiently prioritized or guideline-nuanced.
